answers.core: Ternary operator is a syntax-level feature. It affects how code is written and parsed, which can’t be handled by an external asset or plugin. Add-ons can't modify core language grammar or introduce new operators.
answers.workaround:
Workarounds:

`variable = "foo" if is_active else "bar"`

```
var variable
if is_active:
  variable = "foo"
else:
  variable = "bar"
```

both options are harder to read compared to a proper ternary, especially when chaining or nesting conditions. So while it’s technically possible to work around it, the current alternatives are more cluttered and break code flow

title: Add a new ternary operator to complement the existing `... if ... else ...`
